overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of three approaches to regulating AI. You'll be asked about the EU's risk levels and timetable, the US federal and state picture and preemption, China's measures, and the case for and against each model.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Under the EU's AI Act, what mainly determines which risk level an AI system falls into?

options.html: The size of the company that built it
options.text: The size of the company that built it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The Act's four levels aren't based on company size. They sort systems by what they're used for, so the same software can fall in different levels.

options.html: The use the system is put to
options.text: The use the system is put to
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The four levels sort uses. A sorting system is minimal risk as a spam filter and high risk when it ranks job applicants.

options.html: The country where it was developed
options.text: The country where it was developed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The Act applies to systems offered in the EU wherever they were built. Its levels sort systems by what they're used for.

options.html: The amount of data it was trained on
options.text: The amount of data it was trained on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Training data volume doesn't set the level. The four levels sort systems by what they're used for.

forms.stemHtml: As of October 2026, what did the EU's 2026 amendment to the AI Act do to the duties for high-risk systems?

options.html: It repealed them and left only the bans
options.text: It repealed them and left only the bans
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The duties weren't repealed. The amendment postponed them to December 2027 and August 2028.

options.html: It brought them forward to early 2026
options.text: It brought them forward to early 2026
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The amendment moved the dates later. The duties now apply from December 2027 and August 2028.

options.html: It turned them into a voluntary code
options.text: It turned them into a voluntary code
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The voluntary code of practice concerns general-purpose models. The high-risk duties remain binding and were postponed to December 2027 and August 2028.

options.html: It postponed them to 2027 and 2028
options.text: It postponed them to 2027 and 2028
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The amendment moved the duties for stand-alone high-risk systems to December 2027 and for systems built into products to August 2028.

forms.stemHtml: In the US debate over AI rules, what does "preemption" mean?

options.html: A federal law overriding state laws
options.text: A federal law overriding state laws
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Preemption is the rule that a federal law overrides state laws on the same subject. As of October 2026 Congress had not passed a preemption statute for AI.

options.html: A state law overriding a federal order
options.text: A state law overriding a federal order
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Preemption runs the other way. It's the rule that a federal law overrides state laws on the same subject.

options.html: A president revoking an earlier order
options.text: A president revoking an earlier order
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A president can revoke an executive order, but that isn't preemption. Preemption is the rule that a federal law overrides state laws on the same subject.

options.html: A court striking down a federal statute
options.text: A court striking down a federal statute
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Preemption concerns the relation between federal and state law. It's the rule that a federal law overrides state laws on the same subject.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these do China's measures on generative AI services and on labeling require, according to their translated text? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Training data from lawful sources
options.text: Training data from lawful sources
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The 2023 measures require providers to use data and models that have lawful sources.

options.html: Visible labels on AI-generated content
options.text: Visible labels on AI-generated content
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The 2025 measures require explicit labels that users can clearly perceive, along with implicit labels in the file's data.

options.html: A risk level assigned from a list of four
options.text: A risk level assigned from a list of four
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Sorting uses into four risk levels is the European Union's approach. China's measures set duties on data, content, labeling, and security checks.

options.html: Algorithm filing for services that can shape public opinion
options.text: Algorithm filing for services that can shape public opinion
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Services with public opinion properties or the capacity for social mobilization must pass a security assessment and file their algorithms.

forms.stemHtml: A commentator argues that companies shouldn't have to meet fifty different sets of AI rules. Which model is this an objection to?

options.html: A single risk-based law
options.text: A single risk-based law
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A single law gives one set of rules. The complaint about many differing rules is the patchwork objection to state-level regulation.

options.html: Direct control by state agencies
options.text: Direct control by state agencies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The standard objection to state-led control is its tie to control of information. The complaint about many differing rules is the patchwork objection to state-level regulation.

options.html: Rules made state by state
options.text: Rules made state by state
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the patchwork objection: rules that differ from one state to the next burden developers who must meet all of them.

options.html: Minimal federal regulation
options.text: Minimal federal regulation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The standard objection to minimal regulation is that it leaves safety to companies' own choices. The complaint about many differing rules is the patchwork objection to state-level regulation.

title: Regulatory models: the European Union, the United States, and China
